chapters.title: A Group for a whole procedure
The order points to its policy

capture.application: Claude Code 2.1.330 in macOS Terminal.app, captured with ScreenCaptureKit
capture.scope: One live Claude Code session with the default search_tools and execute_tools over HTTP. A support employee asked one question. The operator entered no tool calls. The client wrote JavaScript and opened refund-review by calling search_tools with its group argument.

editing.first49Seconds: The first scene animates measured startup definition sizes for six synthetic catalogs. The next two scenes display requests and results from two real, model-free PHP MCP SDK sessions. The single-tool session used search_tools and execute_tools. A distinct client exercised the draft groups/list and groups/get methods.
editing.final41Seconds: All nine excerpts show original pixels from one ScreenCaptureKit recording of native Claude Code in macOS Terminal. A PTY relay entered the employee’s question and captured the session through the operator’s recording setup. Claude generated all answers and calls. The operator expanded the genuine transcript. Details are cropped and arranged in workflow order, at normal speed.
editing.modelBehavior: The agent used separate JavaScript blocks. It carried the returned policy ID between MCP calls in one conversation. It accessed the Group through catalog search; the native protocol methods appear in the independent SDK session.
editing.launch: The filmed client was the installed Claude Code executable with native Code Mode and a session-scoped MCP configuration. The separate two-terminal quickstart starts the current client with plain claude.
editing.filmedAttempt: The 41 seconds of terminal excerpts show attempt 4 in docs/evidence/claude-support-review.json. That filmed run used separate generated programs. An independent bare claude launch produced one dependent program and has its own receipt.
editing.captureTiming: The original variable-rate recording was decoded from its first frame into a lossless 25 fps working copy. Holds preserve the actual terminal display while the captured window is static.
